simple.meaning: עָשִׁיר (ʻâshîyr) is a Hebrew word meaning “rich , whether literal or figurative ( noble ).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: עָשִׁיר (H6223) appears 23 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Exodus 30:15, with occurrences in Exodus, Ruth, 2 Samuel, Job, Psalms, and 5 more.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָשִׁיר (H6223) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in עָשִׁיר (H6223) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: עָשִׁיר (ʻâshîyr) / H6223 is traced through Exodus 30:15, Ruth 3:10, 2 Samuel 12:1, 2 Samuel 12:2 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

timeline.evidenceText: The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less, than the half shekel,§ A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces. when they give the offering of Yahweh, to make atonement for your souls.
He said, “You are blessed by Yahweh, my daughter. You have shown more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning, because you didn’t follow young men, whether poor or rich.
Yahweh sent Nathan to David. He came to him, and said to him, “There were two men in one city; the one rich, and the other poor.
The rich man had very many flocks and herds,

A traveler came to the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd, to prepare for the wayfaring man who had come to him, but took the poor man’s lamb, and prepared it for the man who had come to him.”
He lies down rich, but he will not do so again.
The princess inside is all glorious.
My mouth will speak words of wisdom.
The rich man’s wealth is his strong city.
The poor person is shunned even by his own neighbor,
The rich man’s wealth is his strong city,
The poor plead for mercy,
The rich and the poor have this in common:
The rich rule over the poor.
Whoever oppresses the poor for his own increase and whoever gives to the rich,
Better is the poor who walks in his integrity,
The rich man is wise in his own eyes;
When goods increase, those who eat them are increased; and what advantage is there to its owner, except to feast on them with his eyes?
Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in a low place.
Don’t curse the king, no, not in your thoughts;

definitions.full: H6223. ashir עָשִׁיר 23 adjective and noun rich ; — absolute ׳ע Exod 30:15 19 t.; plural absolute עֲשִׁירִים Eccl 10:6 ; construct עֲשִׁירֵי Psa 45:13 ; suffix עֲשִׁירֶיהָ Micah 6:12 ; — adjective masculine 2Sam 12:1 , 4 (opposed to רָאשׁ ), Ruth 3:10 (opposed to רַּל ); usually noun masculine the rich , opposed to רַּל , Prov 10:15 3 t.; opposed to רָשׁ 2Sam 12:2 ; Prov 14:20 4 t.; opposed to אֶבְיוֺן Psa 49:3 ; alone Jer 9:22 ; Micah 6:12 5 t., + עָם עֲשִׁירֵי Psa 45:13 ; ׳ע Isa 53:9 is probably corrupt, compare || רְשָׁעִים ; Bö Ry Di-Kit רַע עשֵֹׁי ; Krochm Gr Che Hpt conjecture רְשָׁעִים for ׳ע and מּשְׁעִים for ׳ר .
